Why would a children's heart surgeon ask Ferrari for help?
It starts at Great Ormond Street Hospital, London.
A baby has just survived heart surgery.
But the danger isn't over.
Now that tiny patient has to move to intensive care.
Every tube, wire and monitor, unplugged and plugged back in.
Several teams. One tiny bed. And things get missed.
Then two of its doctors studied a Formula One pit stop.
Twenty mechanics. One car. A few seconds.
And nobody gets in anyone's way.
So they called Ferrari.
Ferrari's crew studied videos of the hospital's handovers.
Their answer came straight from the pit lane.
One leader, like the lollipop man, runs the whole handover.
Everyone gets one job, in a fixed order.
And a checklist, so nothing gets forgotten.
The result?
Technical errors dropped by forty-two percent.
Missing information, almost cut in half.
A sport chasing tenths of a second taught doctors to protect what matters most.
So next time someone asks you...
